---
title: "Futures and Forwards — Review"
---

## Essential Definitions

| Term | Definition |
|---|---|
| **Futures / Forward** | Agreement to buy/sell an asset at maturity $T$ at price $K$ |
| **Strike $K$** | Delivery price fixed at inception |
| **Maturity $T$** | Mandatory execution date of the contract |
| **Roll-over** | Renewal of the contract before expiry to avoid delivery |
| **Contango** | $F_t >$ expected spot → upward-sloping curve |
| **Backwardation** | $F_t <$ expected spot → downward-sloping curve |

::: {.callout-warning title="Key Pitfall"}
Futures ≠ Options → **obligation** to buy/sell (no choice).
:::

---

## Forwards vs Futures

| Criterion | Forward | Futures |
|---|---|---|
| Market | OTC (bilateral) | Exchange (e.g. CME) |
| Standardisation | No | Yes |
| Delivery dates | Specific | Range of dates |
| Settlement | At maturity | **Daily** |
| Counterparty risk | High | Near zero (clearing house) |
| Close-out | Delivery / cash | Offset before maturity |

---

## Margin Mechanism

**3 components:**

- **Initial margin** — deposit at inception (e.g. 2,000 USD/contract)

- **Maintenance margin** — minimum threshold (e.g. 1,500 USD/contract)

- **Margin call** — if balance < maintenance → top up to **initial** margin

**Daily gain** = $\Delta F_t \times$ contract size

::: {.callout-note title="Example — 2 gold contracts (100 oz), $F_0 = 400$"}
Initial margin: 4,000 USD | Maintenance: 3,000 USD

Day 9 June: balance 2,660 USD < 3,000 → margin call **+1,340 USD**
:::

---

## Pricing Formulas

| Context | Formula |
|---|---|
| No income / dividend / yield | $F_t = S_t \cdot e^{r(T-t)}$ |
| With discrete income $I$ | $F_t = (S_t - I)\cdot e^{r(T-t)}$ |
| With continuous yield $q$ | $F_t = S_t \cdot e^{(r-q)(T-t)}$ |
| Value of an existing contract | $f_t = (F_t - K)\cdot e^{-r(T-t)}$ |
| Simplified value (no dividend) | $f_t = S_t - K\cdot e^{-r(T-t)}$ |

::: {.callout-tip title="Pricing intuition"}
$F_t$ = **replication** cost = spot price carried at the risk-free rate until $T$.
:::

---

## Arbitrage Argument

**If $F_t' > S_t e^{r(T-t)}$** → borrow, buy spot, short futures → profit $F_t' - S_t e^{r(T-t)} > 0$

**If $F_t'' < S_t e^{r(T-t)}$** → short spot, invest, buy futures → profit $S_t e^{r(T-t)} - F_t'' > 0$

→ Conclusion: only $F_t = S_t \cdot e^{r(T-t)}$ eliminates all arbitrage.

---

## Value of a Futures $f_t$

**3 sources of exposure:**

- $S_t$ → direct exposure to the underlying

- $F_t$ → expectations on $S_T$

- $r$ → risk-free rate (via $K \cdot e^{-r(T-t)}$)

::: {.callout-note title="At inception"}
$K = F_0$ → $f_0 = 0$: no premium exchanged at inception.
:::

---

## Contango / Backwardation

| | Contango | Backwardation |
|---|---|---|
| $F_t$ vs expected spot | $F_t >$ spot | $F_t <$ spot |
| Market signal | Expected price ↑, high carry | Expected price ↓, immediate demand ↑ |
| Curve | Upward-sloping | Downward-sloping |

::: {.callout-warning title="Universal property"}
In **all** cases: $F_T \xrightarrow[]{t \to T} S_T$ (convergence at maturity).
:::

---

## Numerical Example — Zero-Coupon Bond (Hull 3.5)

- $S_0 = 930$ USD, $r = 6\%$, $T = 4/12$ year

$$F_0 = 930 \cdot e^{0{,}06 \times \frac{4}{12}} \approx 948{,}79 \text{ USD}$$

---

## Pitfalls & Critical Points

- **Futures ≠ Option**: no choice, firm obligation

- **Margin call** → top up to *initial* margin (not maintenance)

- **$q > 0$ income** → $F_t$ decreases; **$q > 0$ storage cost** → $F_t$ increases

- **$f_0 = 0$** always at inception

- **Convergence** $F_T = S_T$ always holds at maturity
